digest.component_or_area: rebar project code-review criterion authoring and calibration
propositions: A project-owned code-review criterion must enforce four-phase architecture boundaries by detecting when Pass 1 assigns validity/impact/severity/confidence or prescribes fixes, Pass 2 discovers new findings or decides outcomes, Pass 3 applies LLM judgment instead of deterministic thresholds, or Pass 4 overturns findings or dictates implementations.
The criterion must emit grounded, evidence-based findings without severity, confidence, or remediation instructions, using single-turn execution and returning structured code_review_findings.

A balanced 12-case eval corpus (RP-F1..F6 must fire; RP-N1..N6 must not fire) must achieve recall 1.0, false-accept 0.0, agreement 1.0, per-case stability >= 2/3, and Cohen kappa >= 0.70 across three live calibration runs.
Operative instructions (not documentation, tests, examples, or unchanged grandfathered context) must identifiably belong to a single phase; unclear ownership triggers abstention.
Routing must activate the criterion with exec: 1-TURN, block_threshold: 0.90, and blocking_enabled: false in .rebar/criteria_routing.json.

The committed implementation must change only project-owned .rebar/ prompt/routing/eval assets, .gitignore, criterion tests, and docs/llm-framework.md dogfood subsection, with all three live evaluation runs recorded showing perfect calibration metrics.
